title: Primary 4 Rectangles and Squares
seo_title: P4 Rectangles and Squares Worksheets: Free Primary 4 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Properties of rectangle and square, excluding diagonal properties
meta_desc: Free P4 maths practice on rectangles and squares: properties, unknown sides and angles, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A rectangle has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal. A square also has 4 equal sides.
key_sub: ABCD is a rectangle and ∠BAE = 35°, so ∠EAD = 90° − 35° = 55°.
body_html:
What is a rectangle? What is a square?

A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 right angles. Its opposite sides are equal and parallel.

A square is a rectangle with 4 equal sides. So a square is a special rectangle.

A small square at a corner shows a right angle. Sides with the same marks are equal.

Properties

RectangleSquare
Right angles4 (each 90°)4 (each 90°)
Equal sidesopposite sides equalall 4 sides equal
Parallel sides2 pairs2 pairs
Angles add up to360°360°

We write ∠ABC for the angle at B. The middle letter is the corner. // means “is parallel to” and ⊥ means “is perpendicular to”.

Find unknown sides

Use “opposite sides are equal”. For a square, all 4 sides are equal.

Example 1

ABCD is a rectangle. AB = 12 cm and BC = 7 cm. Find DC and the perimeter.

DC is opposite AB, so DC = 12 cm. Perimeter = 12 + 7 + 12 + 7 = 38 cm.

Answer: DC = 12 cm, perimeter 38 cm

Example 2

The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. Find one side.

A square has 4 equal sides. 36 ÷ 4 = 9.

Answer: 9 cm

Find unknown angles

Each corner of a rectangle or square is 90°. When a line splits a corner, the parts add up to 90°.

Example 3

ABCD is a rectangle. ∠BAE = 35°. Find ∠EAD.

∠BAD = 90°. ∠EAD = 90° − 35° = 55°.

Answer: 55°

Word problems with a model

Half the perimeter is one length + one breadth. Draw the length and breadth as bars, then find 1 unit.

Example 4

The length of a rectangle is twice its breadth. Its perimeter is 36 cm. Find its breadth.

Length + breadth = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 cm. 3 units = 18 cm, so 1 unit = 6 cm.

Answer: 6 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
“A turned square is a diamond, not a square.”Check the sides and angles. Turning a shape does not change it
“A rectangle has 4 equal sides.”Only opposite sides are equal. Only a square has 4 equal sides
“A square is not a rectangle.”A square has 4 right angles, so it is a special rectangle
Using 180° for a cornerA corner of a rectangle is 90°. Subtract from 90°, not 180°
Guessing 45° when a line splits a cornerA line from a corner does not always split it equally. Use the given angle
Perimeter ÷ 2 for a side of a squareA square has 4 sides. Divide the perimeter by 4

faq.q: What do P4 students learn about rectangles and squares?
faq.a: In Primary 4, students learn that a rectangle has 4 right angles with opposite sides equal and parallel, and that a square also has 4 equal sides. They use these properties to find unknown sides and angles.
Yes. A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal and parallel, so it is a special rectangle with 4 equal sides. A rectangle is a square only when all its sides are equal.

faq.q: How do I find an unknown angle in a rectangle?
faq.a: Every corner of a rectangle is 90°, so subtract the given angle from 90°. For example, if ∠BAE = 35°, then ∠EAD = 90° − 35° = 55°.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with rectangles and squares?
faq.a: Many children think a square standing on its corner is a “diamond” and not a square, or that a rectangle has 4 equal sides. Checking the right angles and the equal sides clears up both mistakes.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: neither a rectangle nor a square
a square, but not a rectangle
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: Opposite sides are equal and parallel, but there are no right angles. It is neither a rectangle nor a square.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: a square, but not a rectangle
neither a rectangle nor a square
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: It has 4 right angles, and the long sides are different from the short sides. Standing up tall does not matter: it is a rectangle, but not a square.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: a square, but not a rectangle
neither a rectangle nor a square
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: Its 4 sides are equal, but it has no right angles. A square must have 4 right angles, so this is neither a rectangle nor a square.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: neither a rectangle nor a square
a square, but not a rectangle
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: It looks almost like a square, but the sides are 7 cm and 6 cm. The sides are not all equal, so it is a rectangle, but not a square.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: a square, but not a rectangle
neither a rectangle nor a square
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: It is turned, but it still has 4 right angles and 2 pairs of equal sides. It is a rectangle, but not a square.

items.q: A shape has 4 right angles. Two sides are 9 cm and two sides are 4 cm. What is it?
c: neither a rectangle nor a square
a square, but not a rectangle
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: 4 right angles make a rectangle. The sides are not all equal, so it is not a square.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: neither a rectangle nor a square
a square, but not a rectangle
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: It stands on a corner, but it still has 4 right angles and 4 equal sides. It is a square. Some people call it a “diamond”, but turning a shape does not change it.

items.q: Which shape is a rectangle, but not a square?
items.e: A has 4 right angles, but its long and short sides are different. Two of the others are squares, and the rhombus has no right angles.

items.q: Is every rectangle a square?
c: Yes, its opposite sides are equal
No, a rectangle has no right angles
No, its 4 sides may not all be equal
items.e: A square needs 4 equal sides. A rectangle such as 9 cm by 4 cm has 4 right angles but its sides are not all equal.

items.q: A shape has 4 right angles. All its sides are 8 cm. What is it?
c: a rectangle, but not a square
a square, but not a rectangle
neither a rectangle nor a square
items.e: 4 right angles and 4 equal sides make a square.

items.q: Which shape is NOT a rectangle?
items.e: B has no right angles, so it is not a rectangle. The square is a rectangle too, and the turned rectangle is still a rectangle.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: a rectangle, but not a square
neither a rectangle nor a square
a square, but not a rectangle
items.e: Only 2 of its angles are right angles, and only 1 pair of sides is parallel. It is neither a rectangle nor a square.

items.q: Is every square a rectangle?
c: No, a square has no right angles
Yes, it has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal
No, a rectangle must have 2 long sides and 2 short sides
Only when the square is not turned
items.e: A rectangle has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal. A square has all of this, so a square is a special rectangle.

items.q: A shape has 4 sides of 5 cm, but it has no right angles. What is it?
c: a square, but not a rectangle
a rectangle, but not a square
neither a rectangle nor a square
items.e: Equal sides are not enough. A square and a rectangle must have 4 right angles.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: a square, but not a rectangle
a rectangle, but not a square
neither a rectangle nor a square
items.e: It stands on a corner like a turned square, but its angles are not right angles. It is neither a rectangle nor a square.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: neither a rectangle nor a square
a square, but not a rectangle
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: It is turned a little, but it has 4 right angles and 4 equal sides. It is a square.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: a square, but not a rectangle
neither a rectangle nor a square
a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: It has 4 right angles. Opposite sides are equal, but the long sides and short sides are different. It is a rectangle, but not a square.

items.q: Which shape is a square?
items.e: C has 4 right angles and 4 equal sides. It is turned, but it is still a square. The rhombus has equal sides but no right angles.

items.q: The marks show right angles and equal sides. What is this shape?
c: a rectangle, but not a square
a square, but not a rectangle
neither a rectangle nor a square
items.e: It has 4 right angles and 4 equal sides, so it is a square. (A square is also a rectangle.)

items.q: Siti turns a square card so that it stands on one corner. What shape is the card now?
c: a rectangle, but not a square
items.e: Turning a shape does not change its sides or angles. It still has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles.

items.q: Which is true about every square, but NOT about every rectangle?
items.e: Both shapes have 4 right angles and opposite sides equal and parallel. Only a square must have 4 equal sides.

items.q: Which shape has opposite sides parallel, 4 right angles and 4 equal sides?
c: a rhombus that is not a square
a rectangle that is not a square
items.e: 4 right angles and opposite sides parallel make a rectangle. With 4 equal sides as well, it is a square.

items.q: Which is true about every rectangle?
c: It has only 1 pair of parallel sides
items.e: Every rectangle has 4 right angles, and its opposite sides are equal and parallel. Only a square has 4 equal sides.

items.q: PQRS is a square. Which angle is ∠PQR?
items.e: The middle letter tells you the corner. ∠PQR is the angle at Q, and it is 90°.

items.q: What do the 4 angles of a rectangle add up to?
items.e: There are 4 right angles: 90° + 90° + 90° + 90° = 360°.

items.q: WXYZ is a square. Which side is parallel to WX?
items.e: Turning the square does not change it. The side opposite WX is ZY, so WX // ZY.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Which statement is true?
items.e: AB and DC are opposite sides, so they are parallel: AB // DC. AB and BC meet at a right angle, so they are not parallel.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Which statement is true?
items.e: AD and DC meet at D, and ∠ADC = 90°, so AD ⊥ DC. AD and BC are opposite sides, so they are parallel.

items.q: How many right angles does a rectangle have?
items.e: Every corner of a rectangle is a right angle (90°), so it has 4 right angles.

items.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a square have?
items.e: A square has 2 pairs of opposite sides. Each pair is parallel, so there are 2 pairs.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Which two sides are perpendicular?
items.e: Sides that meet at a right angle are perpendicular. AB and BC meet at B, so AB ⊥ BC. AB and DC are parallel.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Which side is equal in length to AD?
items.e: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. AD and BC are opposite each other, so AD = BC.

items.q: Ethan says, “A rectangle has 4 equal sides.” What is wrong?
c: A rectangle has no equal sides
Only opposite sides must be equal
items.e: In a rectangle, the 2 long sides are equal and the 2 short sides are equal. Only a square has 4 equal sides.

items.q: KLMN is a rectangle. What is the size of ∠KLM?
items.e: Every angle of a rectangle is 90°, even when the rectangle is turned. ∠KLM is the angle at L.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Which side is parallel to AB?
items.e: In a rectangle, opposite sides are parallel. The side opposite AB is DC, so AB // DC.

items.q: Which is NOT true about every rectangle?
items.e: Only opposite sides of a rectangle must be equal. A rectangle 10 cm by 4 cm does not have 4 equal sides.

items.q: PQRS is a square. Which sides are equal to PQ?
items.e: All 4 sides of a square are equal, so QR, RS and SP are all equal to PQ.

items.q: Priya draws a line from A to C. She says ∠BAC must be 45°. Is she right?
c: No, the line does not always cut ∠BAD into equal parts
Yes, a line from a corner always makes 45°
items.e: We only know that ∠BAD = 90°. In this long rectangle, AC is much closer to AB than to AD, so ∠BAC is smaller than 45°. Do not guess 45°.

items.q: What is the size of each angle of a square?
items.e: Every angle of a square is a right angle, and a right angle is 90°.

items.q: A shape has 4 equal sides, but its angles are not right angles. Is it a square?
c: No, a square has only 2 equal sides
Yes, if it stands on a corner
No, a square must have 4 right angles
items.e: A square needs 4 equal sides AND 4 right angles. This shape is a rhombus, not a square.

items.q: PQRS is a square. Find the length of QR.
items.e: All sides of a square are equal, so QR = PQ = 9 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. AEFD and EBCF are rectangles. Find the length of EF.
items.e: EF and AD are opposite sides of the rectangle AEFD, so EF = AD = 9 cm.

items.q: The perimeter of a square is 36 cm. Find the length of one side.
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides. 36 ÷ 4 = 9, so each side is 9 cm. (Do not divide by 2.)

items.q: A square has the same perimeter as a rectangle 10 cm by 6 cm. Find the length of one side of the square.
items.e: Perimeter of the rectangle = 10 + 6 + 10 + 6 = 32 cm. Side of the square = 32 ÷ 4 = 8 cm.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 30 cm. Its length is 9 cm. Find its breadth.
items.e: Length + breadth = half the perimeter = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 cm. Breadth = 15 − 9 = 6 cm.

items.q: A rectangle is made of 2 equal squares. Each square has sides of 7 cm. Find the length of the rectangle.
items.e: The length is 2 sides of a square: 7 + 7 = 14 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. E is a point on DC. Find the length of DE.
items.e: DC = AB = 20 cm. DE = 20 − 12 = 8 cm.

items.q: The perimeter of a square is 52 cm. Find the length of one side.
items.e: 52 ÷ 4 = 13, so each side is 13 cm.

items.q: A rectangle has a perimeter of 46 cm. Its breadth is 8 cm. Find its length.
items.e: Length + breadth = 46 ÷ 2 = 23 cm. Length = 23 − 8 = 15 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a square of side 8 cm. BEFC is a rectangle. Find the length of AE.
items.e: AB is a side of the square, so AB = 8 cm. AE = AB + BE = 8 + 5 = 13 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a square of side 9 cm. BEFC is a rectangle. Find the length of EF.
items.e: EF is opposite BC in the rectangle BEFC, so EF = BC. BC is a side of the square, so EF = 9 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Its perimeter is 40 cm. Find BC.
ABCD is a rectangle. Find the length of AD.
items.e: AD is opposite BC, so AD = BC = 7 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. E is a point on AB. Find the length of DC.
items.e: AB = 5 + 9 = 14 cm. DC is opposite AB, so DC = 14 cm.

items.q: A rectangle has a breadth of 9 cm. Its length is 4 cm more than its breadth. Find its perimeter.
items.e: Length = 9 + 4 = 13 cm. Perimeter = 13 + 9 + 13 + 9 = 44 cm.

items.q: This rectangle is made of 3 equal squares. It is 24 cm long. Find the length of one side of a square.
items.e: The length is made of 3 equal sides: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 cm. (Not 24 ÷ 4: there are 3 squares in the row.)

items.q: The length of rectangle ABCD is 3 times its breadth. Its breadth, BC, is 7 cm. Find its length, AB.
items.e: Length = 3 × 7 = 21 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. Find the length of DC.
items.e: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. DC is opposite AB, so DC = 14 cm.

items.q: 4 equal squares with sides of 5 cm are put in a row to make a rectangle. Find the perimeter of the rectangle.
items.e: The rectangle is 4 × 5 = 20 cm long and 5 cm wide. Perimeter = 20 + 5 + 20 + 5 = 50 cm. (80 cm counts the sides inside the rectangle too.)

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. AEFD is a square. Find the length of EB.
items.e: AE is a side of the square, so AE = AD = 6 cm. EB = 15 − 6 = 9 cm.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠BAE = 25° and ∠FAD = 30°. Find ∠EAF.
items.e: The 3 angles at A make a right angle. ∠EAF = 90° − 25° − 30° = 35°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠BAE = 34°. Find ∠EAD.
items.e: The angle at A is a right angle, 90°. ∠EAD = 90° − 34° = 56°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠EAD = 52°. Find ∠BAE.
items.e: The angle at A is a right angle, 90°. ∠BAE = 90° − 52° = 38°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠EDC = 36°. Find ∠ADE.
items.e: The angle at D is a right angle, 90°. ∠ADE = 90° − 36° = 54°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. A line AE splits ∠BAD into two parts. ∠BAE is 4 times as large as ∠EAD. Find ∠BAE.
items.e: ∠BAE is 4 units and ∠EAD is 1 unit. 5 units = 90°, so 1 unit = 18°. ∠BAE = 4 × 18° = 72°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. A line AE splits ∠BAD into two parts. ∠BAE is twice as large as ∠EAD. Find ∠EAD.
items.e: ∠BAE is 2 units and ∠EAD is 1 unit. 3 units = 90°, so 1 unit = 30°. ∠EAD = 30°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠ADE = 58°. Find ∠EDC.
items.e: The angle at D is a right angle, 90°. ∠EDC = 90° − 58° = 32°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠EBA = 63°. Find ∠CBE.
items.e: The angle at B is a right angle, 90°. ∠CBE = 90° − 63° = 27°.

items.q: ABCD is a square. ∠EDC = 55°. Find ∠ADE.
items.e: Every angle of a square is 90°. ∠ADE = 90° − 55° = 35°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠BAE = 28° and ∠EDC = 26°. Find ∠ADE.
items.e: Look at corner D. ∠ADC = 90°, so ∠ADE = 90° − 26° = 64°. The 28° angle is at A, not at D.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠CBE = 40°. Find ∠EBA.
items.e: The angle at B is a right angle, 90°. ∠EBA = 90° − 40° = 50°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠DCE = 28°. Find ∠ECB.
items.e: The angle at C is a right angle, 90°. ∠ECB = 90° − 28° = 62°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠BAE = 32° and ∠FAD = 21°. Find ∠EAF.
items.e: The 3 angles at A make a right angle. ∠EAF = 90° − 32° − 21° = 37°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. A line BE splits ∠ABC into two equal angles. Find ∠ABE.
items.e: ∠ABC = 90°. Two equal parts: 90° ÷ 2 = 45°.

items.q: ABCD is a square. ∠BAE = 62°. Find ∠EAD.
items.e: Every angle of a square is 90°. ∠EAD = 90° − 62° = 28°.

items.q: ABCD is a square. ∠EBA = 33°. Find ∠CBE.
items.e: Every angle of a square is 90°. ∠CBE = 90° − 33° = 57°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠CBE = 27° and ∠FBA = 26°. Find ∠EBF.
items.e: The 3 angles at B make a right angle. ∠EBF = 90° − 27° − 26° = 37°.

items.q: ABCD is a square that has been turned. ∠BAE = 36°. Find ∠EAD.
items.e: Turning does not change the angles. ∠BAD is still 90°, so ∠EAD = 90° − 36° = 54°.

items.q: ABCD is a square. A line AE splits ∠BAD into two parts. ∠BAE is 20° more than ∠EAD. Find ∠EAD.
items.e: Take away the extra 20°: 90° − 20° = 70°. The two equal parts are 70° ÷ 2 = 35°. ∠EAD = 35° and ∠BAE = 55°.

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. ∠ECB = 47°. Find ∠DCE.
items.e: The angle at C is a right angle, 90°. ∠DCE = 90° − 47° = 43°.

items.q: On Sports Day, Primary 4 students run 3 times round a rectangular field. The field is 90 m long and 50 m wide. How far do they run?
Sarah bends a 48 cm piece of wire to make a rectangle 15 cm long. How wide is the rectangle?
items.e: Length + breadth = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 cm. Breadth = 24 − 15 = 9 cm.

items.q: Hui Min has a square piece of paper. Its perimeter is 64 cm. What is the length of one side?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides: 64 ÷ 4 = 16 cm.

items.q: Ryan puts 4 equal square stickers in a row with no gaps. The rectangle formed has a perimeter of 50 cm. What is the length of one side of a sticker?
items.e: Go round the rectangle: 4 sides along the top, 4 along the bottom and 1 at each end. That is 10 sides. 50 ÷ 10 = 5 cm.

items.q: A rectangular gate has a support bar from one corner. The bar makes an angle of 35° with the top edge. What angle does it make with the side edge?
items.e: The corner of the gate is a right angle. 90° − 35° = 55°.

items.q: A rectangular plot in a community garden is 12 m long and 7 m wide. Mr Tan puts a fence all around it. How long is the fence?
items.e: Perimeter = 12 + 7 + 12 + 7 = 38 m.

items.q: A rectangular poster for Children's Day has a perimeter of 120 cm. Its length is 20 cm longer than its breadth. Find its breadth.
items.e: Length + breadth = 120 ÷ 2 = 60 cm. 2 units = 60 − 20 = 40 cm, so 1 unit = 20 cm. The breadth is 20 cm.

items.q: The length of a rectangle is 3 times its breadth. Its perimeter is 64 cm. Find its breadth.
items.e: Length + breadth = 64 ÷ 2 = 32 cm. From the model, 4 units = 32 cm, so 1 unit = 8 cm. The breadth is 8 cm.

items.q: Mdm Wong sews lace around a rectangular tablecloth. The tablecloth is 2 m long and 1 m 20 cm wide. How much lace does she need?
The length of a rectangle is 6 cm longer than its breadth. Its perimeter is 40 cm. Find its length.
items.e: Length + breadth = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 cm. 2 units = 20 − 6 = 14 cm, so 1 unit = 7 cm. Length = 7 + 6 = 13 cm.

items.q: Kumar glues a ribbon around the edge of a rectangular photo frame. The frame is 25 cm long and 18 cm wide. How much ribbon does he need?
items.e: Perimeter = 25 + 18 + 25 + 18 = 86 cm. (43 cm is only one length and one breadth.)

items.q: Devi ties a ribbon around a rectangular card 20 cm by 12 cm. She also needs 8 cm more for a bow. How much ribbon does she need in all?
items.e: Perimeter = 20 + 12 + 20 + 12 = 64 cm. Add the bow: 64 + 8 = 72 cm.

items.q: A square window has a perimeter of 4 m 80 cm. How long is one side, in centimetres?
items.e: 4 m 80 cm = 480 cm. One side = 480 ÷ 4 = 120 cm.

items.q: A square playground has sides of 25 m. A fence is put along 3 of its sides. The fourth side is a wall. How long is the fence?
items.e: The fence covers 3 equal sides: 3 × 25 = 75 m.

items.q: Nurul bends a 48 cm piece of wire to make a square. What is the length of one side of the square?
items.e: The wire goes all around the square: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm.

items.q: Chloe hangs a square photo frame on a nail by one corner, so it looks like a diamond. What is the size of each angle of the frame?
items.e: It is still a square, only turned. Every angle of a square is 90°.

items.q: Farah paints a straight line from corner A of a square tile ABCD. ∠BAE = 52°. Find ∠EAD.
items.e: ∠BAD is a right angle. ∠EAD = 90° − 52° = 38°.

items.q: The breadth of a rectangle is half its length. Its perimeter is 54 cm. Find its length.
items.e: Length + breadth = 54 ÷ 2 = 27 cm. 3 units = 27 cm, so 1 unit = 9 cm. Length = 2 units = 18 cm.

items.q: Mei Ling joins 2 equal square tiles to make a rectangle. Each square has a perimeter of 20 cm. What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
items.e: Each side of a square is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm. The rectangle is 10 cm by 5 cm. Perimeter = 10 + 5 + 10 + 5 = 30 cm. (40 cm counts the side in the middle twice.)

items.q: A rectangular notice board at the HDB void deck is 3 m long. Its perimeter is 8 m. How wide is the notice board?
items.e: Length + breadth = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 m. Breadth = 4 − 3 = 1 m. (5 m is 8 − 3: it forgets that there are 2 lengths.)
